Definition: Tachath, the name of a place in the Desert, also of three Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Tachath is the name of a place in the wilderness, where Israel camped on the march from Egypt, and of three Israelites: a Kohathite Levite, son of Assir, and two men of Ephraim's line. The place is named in the march list, and the men in the genealogies, and the spelling is the same for all of them. The word underneath the name means below, and the camp at Tachath sat low in the desert road.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the shared spelling is worth noting plainly: one word covers a desert camp and three men, and the Bible does not confuse them, even when the spelling is the same.
